evidence: create-product-dto.ts: CreateProductDto only declares @IsString name/description and @IsNumber price. Its doc comment says the domain invariants live in the Name/Price validators, not in the DTO.
create-product.command.ts: CreateProductCommand(product: CreateProductDto) only copies name, description and price. It holds no logic.

create-product.service.ts: CreateProductService.execute builds new CreateProductCommand(dto) and sends it through commandBus.execute, so it uses the CQRS abstraction and doesn't call the handler directly.

create-product.command-handler.ts: CreateProductCommandHandler.execute calls Product.create(Name.create, Description.create, Price.create) and checks product.isValid / brokenRules.getBrokenRules(). It relies on the domain's invariants rather than copying them.
The index.ts barrel re-exports all four files as one use-case module.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files serve one concern: the create-product use case. The flow runs from the DTO to the service, then to the command, then through the command bus to the handler, which builds the aggregate and saves it. The DTO checks only the structure of the request (field types). The domain invariants (Name length, positive Price) stay in the value objects and the aggregate. The handler doesn't re-check them. It reads the aggregate's brokenRules, so each rule lives in one place. The service uses the CQRS abstraction: it builds the command and sends it through the CommandBus instead of calling the handler directly. The handler injects the concrete infrastructure ProductRepository, but that is an import-direction / layer-dependency question and is out of scope here. I found no split into unrelated concerns, no duplicated invariants and no bypass of the module's own abstractions.
